requested_outcome: The vacation accessibility filter returns every catalog place carrying the verified accessibility attribute instead of an incorrect empty result.
natural_destination: VII vacation search on desktop and mobile with accessible=1, including the filter drawer preview and applied results.
authorization_boundary: Local diagnosis, code repair, tests and commit are authorized. Public deployment is not authorized by this request.

lesson_bundle.reason: The visible accessibility filter promises a real action but currently returns a false empty result.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Apply and preview states must both use the canonical catalog filter identity and return verified matching places.

lesson_bundle.reason: The defect is in shared filtering logic and cannot be closed from the reported screenshot alone.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Verify compact payload preservation, applied results, draft preview, reload persistence and adjacent feature filters.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The chip is corrected but the filter drawer preview still reports zero.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Replace every accessibility predicate in both applied and draft filtering paths.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Source assertion and functional test cover all four shared call sites.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The repair matches free text but ignores the canonical API-derived filter ID after payload compaction.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Use matchesVacationSearchFilter, which prioritizes searchFilterIds and only then falls back to source text.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: A compact property whose visible features omit accessibility still matches accessible through searchFilterIds.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Accessibility starts working but another vacation feature filter regresses.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Run the complete vacation filter and compact-payload regression families plus the production build.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Focused and affected-family test suites pass without modifying unrelated filter identities.

sources.label: User screenshot showing the false zero-result state with accessibility selected
Canonical API-derived filter IDs retained in the compact search payload

midpoint_gate.trigger: After reproducing the mismatch between canonical accessible IDs and visible feature labels, before editing the UI filter.
checks: Count source and projected places with the accessible ID
Count projected places that pass the current visible-feature predicate
Confirm the mismatch explains the exact empty state

attack_questions: Does a compact card with no visible accessibility label still match its verified accessible ID?
Do both applied and draft-preview paths use the same canonical predicate?
Do unrelated pool, spa and additional feature filters still pass their contracts?
Does accessible=1 persist and recover the same result set after reload?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Local desktop and mobile search opened with accessible=1 and a nonzero result count matching the catalog identity count.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Focused payload, filter contract, URL persistence and production build results.

effectiveness.baseline: Before repair, 4 of 573 vacation properties carried accessible in searchFilterIds, while the search page returned 0 because it inspected only three display features.
effectiveness.target: All 4 verified accessible properties survive compact projection and both UI filter paths, with zero regressions in the focused family.
